data.exact_reserve_text: On 14 February 2018, the managing agency entered in to an external reinsurance to close agreement ('RITC') for each of the three run-off years, which contained the specialist sports and leisure book managed by the previous owners. As a result, the assets and liabilities of these years within the balance sheet as at 31 December 2017, were transferred to Syndicate 3330's 2018 year of account managed by Coverys Managing Agency Limited. The claims provisions carried forward also include significant reserving added to the professional indemnity book during 2018, as referred to in the Claims environment section above. This class accounts for 45% of the carried forward net provisions for the 2016 pure year of account.

Assets and liabilities of the run-off years were transferred out as a result of an external RITC; reflected in the claims reconciliation as a gross external RITC transfer of 37,982 (thousands).
Significant reserves were added to the professional indemnity book during 2018; this class accounts for 45% of the carried forward net provisions for the 2016 pure year of account.

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims reserves at 1 Jan 2018 were GBP 116.773m. During 2018 the syndicate recognised adverse prior-year development on a gross basis of GBP 55.671m (47.7% of opening reserves), driven by reserve strengthening particularly in the professional indemnity/pecuniary loss portfolio following a reserving review and by catastrophe-related development from prior CAT events. In addition an external RITC transferred run-off year assets and liabilities (gross GBP 37.982m) out of the balance sheet. The combined effect was a net increase in gross claims outstanding to GBP 142.035m at 31 Dec 2018.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development gross figure taken from claims outstanding reconciliation line 'Claims incurred in prior underwriting years' (gross GBP 55,671k) in Note 3 - this is the most explicit gross prior-year movement available in the file. The claims reconciliation also includes a gross external RITC transfer of GBP 37,982k which materially affects comparatives and the claims outstanding movement; this RITC distorts simple movements and makes a claims-triangle based PYD calculation unreliable. No gross claims development triangle was available in the provided pages. Where class-level reserve movements were not explicitly quantified, amounts are left null and direction inferred from narrative.
